- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., +0.11 to +0.17) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices during negative sentiment periods (e.g., -0.28 to -0.33) — model is overly optimistic, fails to reflect bearish momentum.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts — especially when sentiment turns negative, forecast lags and drops too slowly.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after recent peaks, ignoring historical volatility and mean reversion patterns.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early days of a new trend (e.g., 1–3 days after sentiment shift) — model overweights recent momentum.
- When sentiment is stable or near-zero, model tends to overfit recent price trends — underestimates volatility and mean reversion.
- Forecast should adjust downward if sentiment is negative and price is above 74.00 — model often ignores sentiment-driven corrections.
- Avoid overconfidence in “recent high” as a signal — model frequently assumes continuation, ignoring sentiment decay or reversal.
